samples.question: The picture shows one dark conduit of constant thickness on a plain white background. A solid green square marks the port. From the port a short stem runs to a single junction, where the conduit splits into exactly two arms and never splits again. Each arm leaves the junction along a straight base leg, turns, and then doubles back past the junction, so the arm that leaves the junction on one side always finishes on the opposite side: where a pad sits never tells you which arm carries it, and the direction a vane points never tells you where its pad sits. Each arm ends on one small coloured pad; one pad is blue and one pad is orange. Two small dark triangles, the vanes, float beside the conduit, exactly one of them beside each arm's base leg, and every vane is separated from the ink by clear background. A vane belongs to the base leg it lies closest to. A vane opens its arm when its point aims away from the junction along that base leg, and seals its arm when its point aims back toward the junction. Exactly one of the two vanes opens its arm. Travel begins at the green port, runs along the stem to the junction, and may then continue only along an arm whose vane is open; a sealed arm may never be entered. All light gray shapes anywhere in the picture are decoration and mean nothing. Which coloured pad can be reached from the green port? Answer blue or orange.
